capture: s0 + fintech layer — Premium Disruption Assistance

MATERIAL_QUALIFICATION_of_F57.F57_as_stated: Traced across five competitors, the traveller's protection degrades at every hop and nobody holds the whole chain. Recorded as 'the clearest statement of Luma's opportunity produced by this round'.
MATERIAL_QUALIFICATION_of_F57.what_Hopper_shows: One competitor sells exactly that ownership, as a named product.
MATERIAL_QUALIFICATION_of_F57.evidence_verbatim: If your flight is delayed or canceled, instantly rebook on any airline. If you are not happy with the rebooking options, get a 100% refund of your flight instead.
MATERIAL_QUALIFICATION_of_F57.the_corrected_position: The gap is NOT that nobody owns the disruption moment. It is that ownership is sold as a PAID ADD-ON, inside an APP, attached to that product's own bookings — rather than being a property of the journey itself.
MATERIAL_QUALIFICATION_of_F57.why_the_correction_matters: F-57 as written would have led Luma to claim an unoccupied space that is in fact occupied by a well-capitalised specialist. The honest version is narrower and far more useful: the question is not whether to own disruption, it is whether owning it is a PRODUCT YOU BUY or a PROPERTY OF THE THING YOU ALREADY BOUGHT.

the_product.name: Premium Disruption Assistance
the_product.core_promise_verbatim: If your flight is delayed or canceled, instantly rebook on any airline. If you are not happy with the rebooking options, get a 100% refund of your flight instead.
the_product.notable_scope: 'rebook on ANY airline' — not restricted to the original carrier. That is materially more than EU 261 obliges an airline to do, and more than Iberia's changes page offers (F-56).
the_product.cost: NOT STATED on this page. A customer review quoted on the page says 'you can rebook it if you pay a small amount' — that is a testimonial, not a price. Recorded as UNKNOWN.
the_product.page_size: 1,631 characters — a thin marketing page, not documentation.

finding_F64_THE_FINTECH_FAMILY.claim: Hopper ships a family of flexibility products, not a single one.
finding_F64_THE_FINTECH_FAMILY.reading: Every one converts an anxiety into a purchasable option. This is the most developed answer to traveller anxiety observed in the round — and it is a FINANCIAL product line, not a UX one.
finding_F64_THE_FINTECH_FAMILY.the_uncomfortable_implication: Expedia monetises anxiety by shaming the decline (F-22). Hopper monetises it by selling the cure as a product family. Both are revenue models built on the same fear Luma proposes to remove. A product that genuinely removes the fear removes the revenue with it. That is a business-model question the scenario does not address.

finding_F65_THE_BROWSER_LIMIT_MEASURED.claim: Hopper's web surface permits search but gates its differentiating products behind the app.

evidence.web_can: Search inputs and buttons present and functional for both stays and flights — 'Search destination', 'Add dates', 'Add guests', 'Departure', 'Destination', 'Add travelers'.
evidence.web_cannot: 'Premium Disruption Assistance' states 'Available in the Hopper app'. Homepage carries 'Scan to download' and 'Get deal alerts on the app'.
evidence.page_shape: Homepage 1,769 DOM nodes / 89 links — by far the thinnest of the six competitors captured. Booking.com 5,393/300, Skyscanner 2,994/446, Kayak 3,657/487.

finding_F65_THE_BROWSER_LIMIT_MEASURED.why_this_was_scheduled_here: ART-024 placed Hopper at position 6 specifically to measure the browser-only limit before more sessions were planned around it. The measurement: the web surface is a functional search plus a marketing site for the app. Every capture of Hopper's actual differentiators — prediction accuracy, price freeze mechanics, the disruption product in use — is UNREACHABLE by this method.
finding_F65_THE_BROWSER_LIMIT_MEASURED.consequence_for_the_plan: Hopper cannot be captured to the same depth as the other sixteen. This must be stated in any comparison rather than letting Hopper look feature-poor because the method could not see it. Recorded as a METHOD limit, not a product finding.
options_for_a_human: capture on a phone with the app installed
accept Hopper as web-surface-only and label every Hopper comparison accordingly

our_product_decision_required: Decision required — the biggest one this round has produced: is disruption protection something Luma SELLS, or something Luma IS? Hopper sells it. Expedia sells the adjacent fear. Iberia acknowledges the moment and abandons it. Booking.com disclaims it. Luma's stated objective — 'reducing travel stress... at every stage' — reads as the second, but the second has no observed revenue model.

Decision required: 'rebook on any airline' is the strongest single promise found in the round. Luma cannot make it without either inventory relationships or a balance sheet to absorb the cost. Which is it buying?

Decision required: how does Luma treat a competitor whose differentiators are app-only? Hopper's web surface understates it. Any Luma comparison built from web capture alone will misjudge its strongest rival on exactly the axis Luma cares most about.
not_observed: the price of Premium Disruption Assistance — the single most important missing number
whether it covers flights NOT booked through Hopper
Price Prediction accuracy claims — the standing vendor-claim caution from the skill applies
Price Freeze — searched for 'price freeze', 'lock in price': NO match on the homepage. Not observed, not absent.
